title: Start tmux through Ghostty login shell
description: Configure Ghostty to automatically start or attach tmux after its shell startup so a newly created server inherits the Ghostty shell environment. Preserve the shared tmux environment contract, document the startup behavior, and validate configuration plus focused startup smoke checks.
notes:
Configured Ghostty to run /bin/zsh -lic before exec tmux new-session -A -s main. Updated shell-environment spec with startup and existing-server environment behavior. Temporary clients and server removed. Existing shared environment adapter preserved.

Removed only the outer exec; inner Zsh exec tmux remains. Reproduced the reported failure using /usr/bin/login -flp ct /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -c with Ghostty's wrapper. Verified the exact corrected config command through that same wrapper in a PTY with a temporary TMUX_TMPDIR and full real tmux configuration: main attached, caller marker/TERM_PROGRAM and interactive STARSHIP_CACHE inherited, temporary server cleaned up, existing tmux server untouched. - launchr: user-agents-only GUI (gui/ domain). Load/unload/enable/disable/run now, form + raw plist, tail logs. https://github.com/scoult/launchr

title: BV work view ownership is advisory setup policy, not a scheduler invariant
description:
{"formatVersion":1,"taskId":"dots-5xaa.2","requestId":"dots-euj3","author":"orange-influential-gorilla","body":"Bee cares because its setup command has taken ownership of three BV view names. The examined runtime does not need `work` to be label-only. Rejecting your extra filters is a design choice in setup, and coupling that choice to installation is what breaks `make`.

Your question was: “why does bee care? i think its a terrible idea if a tool is forcing a config option with no visibility; can we see why this filter is needed?” The exclusions have a useful discovery purpose; that does not establish a need to prohibit customization.

1. **What the exclusions do.** [The label taxonomy](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/docs/beads-labels.md:19) defines `system` as automation-owned coordination/execution records and `busybee-workflow` as generated runs, groups and stages. `work` excludes both; `workflows` selects the latter. Access, assignment and routing for workflow work remain unchanged. Commit `2588b3cf` explicitly says to keep ordinary parent work visible and expose generated workflow work separately. My interpretation: this keeps advisory discovery focused on original work instead of automation records and generated workflow visits. These filters are neither an execution authorization boundary nor filters on native `br` calls; [integration guidance](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/docs/integrations.md:64) says so explicitly.

2. **Who actually consumes `work`.** [Honeybee's prompt](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.hive/bees/honeybee/system_prompt.md:5) requests it for triage, parallel planning and next-pick advice. [Beeswax prime](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/beeswax/src/prime.ts:134) teaches all agents the same ordinary-view convention and states that native Beads owns readiness. In contrast, [Colony's ranking adapter](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/colony/src/ranking.ts:39) invokes `bv --robot-insights --force-full-analysis --db … --format json`, without `--recipe`; it checks selected-source authority and graph completeness. [Scheduling documentation](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/colony/README.md:125) requires full-graph scores, including closed/ephemeral tasks, and supports FIFO without BV. [Hive UI topology](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/hive-ui/server/topology.ts:79) also invokes BV without that recipe. I found no examined Bee/Colony runtime consumer requiring the named `work` view or its label-only shape. Its consumers are advisory instructions; runtime ranking has a separate boundary.

3. **What your extra filters change.** BV v0.25.2 accepts both keys. Its [recipe filter](/Users/ct/dev/vendor/beads_viewer@v0.25.2/pkg/recipe/apply.go:103) intersects all conditions. `status: [open, in_progress]` removes other statuses. `actionable: true` uses [Ready](/Users/ct/dev/vendor/beads_viewer@v0.25.2/pkg/model/readiness.go:173): open/in-progress, not deferred and dependencies satisfied. It can include assigned ongoing work; it is not the stricter claimable predicate. In this version the explicit status list repeats Ready's status restriction. These filters narrow advisory planning/triage input and hide blocked, deferred and historical ordinary work; they can change graph analysis as well as displayed rows because [robot scoping](/Users/ct/dev/vendor/beads_viewer@v0.25.2/cmd/bv/main.go:4903) replaces the issue set with recipe results before output. That is a real view-semantics trade-off, not evidence that Colony needs the broader named view. Readiness retains full-source dependency context, so an excluded blocker is not simply forgotten.

4. **Why installation fails.** Canonical Hive [.bv/recipes.yaml](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/.bv/recipes.yaml:5) contains your two extra keys; its permanent tracker recipe has only the exclusions. [setup.ts](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/colony/src/setup.ts:26) uses strict objects allowing only the exact owned filters and optional description. Thus even valid BV customization fails validation. [Reconciliation](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/colony/src/setup.ts:159) accepts missing defaults or compatible views, upgrades the old `[system]` exclusion, and throws on other shapes. [Preflight](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/colony/src/setup.ts:111) validates both checkout documents before saved-query/file writes, so this conflict causes no Bee setup writes. Earlier installation steps may already have run. [Hive's default mise task](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/mise.toml:5) builds/installs and bootstraps the tracker, then runs `bee setup` unconditionally at line 9. [Dots setup](/Users/ct/dev/dots/boot/setup.sh:38) invokes that default task. The failure therefore propagates into bootstrap. [Setup help](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/lib/colony/src/bee-cli.ts:203) documents owned views, but the error gives only the conflicting name/path and a help pointer, rather than the rejected keys and expected shape.

History: `05b89c5c` introduced Bee setup for its native attention query. `d7e55e9f` added strict `work`/`system` viewer ownership during onboarding improvements. `2588b3cf` added workflow classification and the third view without changing that ownership model. Twelve minutes later, `88e0ff85` (`chore: bv view`) added your two keys; its message supplies no further rationale. These inspected commits establish sequence and intended defaults, not a demonstrated need to reject every narrower view. The architecture's [setup boundary](/Users/ct/dev/projects/hive/docs/architecture.md:91) expressly assigns Bee its attention preset; it does not explain why the generic `work` name must prohibit user filters.

**Advice, pending your decision:** decide who owns the generic view name. Options are to allow user filters while retaining the required exclusions; make Hive's advisory preset explicitly named/selected and leave `work` user-controlled; or deliberately reserve `work` and put customization elsewhere. The last option is the existing temporary `work`/`actionable-work` proposal, not accepted policy. My recommendation is explicit view ownership and separating advisory-view configuration from required installation, with diagnostics showing the actual conflict. Removing your keys alone complies with today's validator but does not resolve your objection.

Architectural evidence, 2026-10-21; topic `bv-work-view-ownership`. Interpretation: discovery defaults, runtime correctness and installation policy had been conflated. Resolution: user paused implementation; ownership and install coupling remain undecided. Guidance gap: defaults/ownership are documented in CLI help, but the necessity of exclusive generic-name ownership and installation failure is unexplained. Action/outcome: source-backed consultation only; previous dots-urme advice to remove filters or use another name is one compatibility option, not proof of accepted intent. Next evidence: the user's ownership decision before any repair resumes.

Evidence window: Hive HEAD `5f8727d4`, the four commits above, supplied report `dots-urme`, both current recipe files and the paused proposal's YAML diff; local tagged BV v0.25.2 source matches the installed version. Only this assigned dots workflow claim, comments, response and completion records change. No independent architecture evidence record was created, as instructed. Parent repair dots-5xaa remains paused and outside this report's completion authority.
